prompt.context: Storm Games is a video game developer focused on computer games. Their main title, King of the Forest, is an online RPG that has been extremely successful. While the game still provides a steady cash flow to Storm Games, growth has stagnated in recent years as the number of new players has decreased significantly and average revenue per user has reached a plateau. Storm Games plans on going public in the near future and, in order to show strong results before the IPO, the company has hired you to develop a strategy to show investors that it can continue to grow.
prompt.question: At a high level, what are the main avenues where the company can potentially increase revenues?

clarifying_info.q: What type of games has Storm Games developed so far?
clarifying_info.a: Storm Games has only developed RPGs for computers.

clarifying_info.q: Has the company decided which alternative to pursue?
clarifying_info.a: At this time, the company is exploring a number of alternatives and has yet to determine the target result.
RPG stands for Role Playing Game.

exhibits.title: Revenues Mobile Game Industry per Segment
exhibits.shows: A stacked bar chart showing annual revenues (in $billions) for the mobile game industry broken down by segment (RPG, Sports, Adventure, Other Genres) from 2014 to 2021 (Forecast). Also shows Average Gross Revenue per Active Player Account per Year for selected segments. A footnote states that distribution platforms (Google Play and App Store) retain a 20% commission over gross revenue.

data.commission_footnote: Distribution platforms retain a 20% commission over gross revenue
data.note: Players may play multiple games per year across different segments; each game requires a unique player account

exhibits.title: Storm Games Estimated Game Development Costs per Segment
exhibits.shows: A grouped bar chart showing estimated game development costs (in $millions) for Storm Games across three segments (RPG, Adventure, Sports), broken down into four cost components: Design, Coding, Marketing, and Legal/Licensing.

framework: Revenue drivers: Average revenue per user (player account) × Number of users (player accounts)
Cost drivers: Investment/development costs (Design, Coding, Marketing, Legal/Licensing) + Fixed costs + Variable costs
Gaming Industry / Market: Size of each segment, industry trends, growth trajectory
Storm Games Capabilities: Expertise to develop games in other segments, synergies with existing RPG know-how, reputational risks

questions.prompt: Brainstorm: What are the main avenues where Storm Games can potentially increase revenues?
questions.guidance: Candidates should identify two broad categories. (1) Increase revenues from current games: raise prices, display in-game ads, expand in-game purchases/merchandise, introduce product placement (e.g., branded in-game characters). (2) Launch new games: branch out to new platforms (mobile) and/or new genres. The case proceeds with option 2 — launching a new mobile game. If the candidate does not identify option 2 independently, guide them toward it.

questions.prompt: Storm Games has decided to develop a new mobile game. Using Exhibit 1, what do you observe about the mobile gaming market and which segment appears most attractive?
questions.guidance: Candidates should note: (1) The overall industry shows a strong growth trend despite a dip in 2021F (explained by Covid-19 pull-forward in 2020). (2) Adventure and Sports are the segments driving growth; RPG has remained relatively stable. (3) Adventure has the second-highest average gross revenue per player account ($9.38) after Sports ($9.69). Best candidates will flag the 20% platform commission footnote as relevant to payback calculations.

questions.prompt: Using Exhibits 1 and 2, calculate how many player accounts Storm Games needs to acquire in each segment to pay back its investment within one year. In which segment should Storm Games invest?
questions.guidance: Candidates must apply the 20% platform commission to convert gross revenue to net revenue, then divide total development cost by net revenue per account. Adventure requires the fewest player accounts (2.40M) and is therefore the most attractive segment on a payback basis despite not having the lowest development cost.

math.setup: Net Revenue per Account = Avg Gross Rev per Account × (1 – 20% commission). Player Accounts needed = Total Development Cost ÷ Net Revenue per Account.
steps: RPG: Net Rev = $7.50 × 0.80 = $6.00 per account; Accounts needed = $15.00M ÷ $6.00 = 2.50M
Adventure: Net Rev = $9.38 × 0.80 = $7.50 per account; Accounts needed = $18.00M ÷ $7.50 = 2.40M
Sports: Net Rev = $9.69 × 0.80 = $7.75 per account; Accounts needed = $20.15M ÷ $7.75 = 2.60M
math.answer: Adventure requires the fewest player accounts (2.40M) to break even within one year, making it the most attractive segment.

brainstorming.prompt: At a high level, what are the main avenues where Storm Games can potentially increase revenues?

categories.name: Increase revenues from current games
ideas: Display periodic in-game ads (similar to TV commercial breaks)
Expand portfolio of in-game purchasable features and merchandise
Introduce product placement where external brands pay for in-game advertising (e.g., a character branded with Coca-Cola)

categories.name: Launch new games
ideas: Develop a new RPG for mobile platforms
Branch out into new genres (Adventure, Sports, Other) for mobile

recommendation: Storm Games should develop an Adventure game for mobile platforms.

Despite lower production costs for a new RPG, the higher average net revenue per player account in the Adventure segment ($7.50 vs. $6.00 for RPG) results in fewer player accounts needed to pay back the investment within one year (2.40M vs. 2.50M for RPG and 2.60M for Sports).
The Adventure segment also shows strong and growing industry revenues, making it strategically attractive ahead of the IPO.
risks: Storm Games has only developed RPG games; it may lack the expertise, creative talent, and resources to effectively develop and market an Adventure game.
Average revenue figures may be misleading — the variance and range of revenues across titles could be wide, and Storm Games' first Adventure title may underperform the average.
If the new Adventure game fails commercially, it could damage Storm Games' brand and reputation, negatively impacting investor sentiment ahead of the IPO.
next_steps: Assess internal capabilities to determine whether Storm Games has the talent and technology to develop a high-quality Adventure game, or whether external hires or studio acquisitions are needed.
Conduct deeper market research on the Adventure segment — competitive landscape, top titles, player demographics, and revenue distribution — to refine revenue projections.
Develop a detailed go-to-market and launch plan to maximize player account acquisition in year one and achieve the payback target.
